title: Lionsgate releases a new trailer for Sunrise on the Reaping
gist: Lionsgate released a trailer for The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping, a Haymitch Abernathy origin story opening November 20, while Laika Studios released the final trailer for its stop-motion feature Wildwood, opening October 23. Limited market relevance beyond franchise-release scheduling and the note that Laika's May teaser drew over 90 million views.

insights.claim: The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping is a sequel to 2023's Ballad of Songbirds and Snakes and a prequel leading into the events of the original 2012 Hunger Games film, opening in theaters on November 20.
insights.speaker: Jennifer Ouellette
insights.so_what: A concrete release date for a major franchise entry in the pre-holiday theatrical window.
insights.locator: Lionsgate has released an action-packed trailer

insights.claim: The film is set in Panem 24 years before the original story and follows a young Haymitch (Joseph Zada) who forms an alliance with fellow tribute Maysilee Donner (Mckenna Grace) and joins a coalition challenging the Capitol's control under President Snow (Ralph Fiennes).
insights.speaker: Jennifer Ouellette
insights.so_what: Establishes the film as an origin story bridging the existing prequel and the original trilogy.
insights.quote: Haymitch risks everything to take down the Games from within the arena — setting in motion the rebellion that will change Panem forever.

insights.claim: The story covers the 50th Hunger Games, the Second Quarter Quell, in which each district is required to send twice as many tributes to compete to the death.
insights.speaker: Jennifer Ouellette
insights.so_what: The doubled-tribute premise is the structural device driving the film's scale versus prior entries.
insights.locator: Haymitch’s fellow District 12 tributes for the 50th Hunger Games

insights.claim: The author notes the film carries an unusual dramatic problem: readers of the books already know Haymitch wins his Games, so 'the suspense and the emotional stakes lie in how he pulls it off—and what he loses in the process.'
insights.speaker: Jennifer Ouellette
insights.so_what: A known-outcome prequel must sell process over plot — a recurring creative constraint in franchise extensions.
insights.quote: the suspense and the emotional stakes lie in how he pulls it off—and what he loses in the process
insights.locator: If you’ve read all the books and seen the films

insights.claim: The cast is stacked with recognizable names in young versions of established roles, including Jesse Plemons as a young cameraman Plutarch, Glenn Close as Drusilla Sickle, Kieran Culkin as a young Caesar Flickerman, Elle Fanning as a young Effie Trinket, Billy Porter as stylist Magno Stift, Maya Hawke as young Wiress and Lili Taylor as young Mags Flanagan.
insights.speaker: Jennifer Ouellette
insights.so_what: Heavy star loading on supporting roles signals a large budget and Lionsgate's commitment to the franchise.
insights.locator: The cast also includes Jesse Plemons as a young cameraman named Plutarch

insights.claim: Jennifer Lawrence and Josh Hutcherson will reprise their roles as Katniss and Peeta, most likely in a flash-forward cameo to set up the segue into the original film.
insights.speaker: Jennifer Ouellette
insights.so_what: Returning original leads is the connective tissue Lionsgate is using to tie the prequel line back to the core trilogy.
insights.locator: Lawrence and Hutcherson will reprise their respective roles

insights.claim: Laika Studios released an extended teaser for its stop-motion animated feature Wildwood in May that racked up over 90 million views, which the author attributes to Laika's stellar reputation and the visuals.
insights.speaker: Jennifer Ouellette
insights.so_what: 90 million teaser views is a concrete pre-release demand signal for a niche animation format.
insights.locator: Laika Studios released an extended teaser for this stop-motion animated film in May

insights.claim: Wildwood follows twelve-year-old Prue McKee, whose baby brother Mac is carried off by a murder of crows, leading her and schoolmate Curtis Mehlberg into a magical Wilderness populated by coyotes, bandits and a mysterious woman named Alexandra who has lost her son.
insights.speaker: Jennifer Ouellette
insights.so_what: Plot summary for readers deciding whether to watch; no market implication.
insights.locator: Twelve-year-old Prue McKee discovers the forest

insights.claim: Wildwood carries a large voice cast including Peyton Elizabeth Lee, Jacob Tremblay, Carey Mulligan, Angela Bassett, Mahershala Ali, Awkwafina, Charlie Day, Amandla Stenberg, Tom Waits and Richard E. Grant, and opens in theaters on October 23.
insights.speaker: Jennifer Ouellette
insights.so_what: A high-profile voice cast plus an October date puts Wildwood in the awards-season animation conversation.

insights.claim: The first full Wildwood trailer, released last month, was set to a haunting cover of Avicii's 'Wake Me Up.'
insights.speaker: Jennifer Ouellette
insights.so_what: Licensed-track trailer cuts remain a standard marketing lever for reaching broader audiences.
insights.locator: The equally gorgeous first full trailer
